original_title: 15 Games We Don’t Believe Anyone Actually Played All the Way Through
summary_en: From notoriously difficult challenges to outright broken experiences, some games demand a level of dedication few players can truly muster. This list dives into titles that test the limits of player patience and perseverance.
ai_analysis: This list explores the ultimate test of a gamer's commitment, mirroring the binge-watching endurance required for the most demanding TV series.

en.title: 10 Games We Bet You Didn't Actually Finish
en.summary: From notoriously difficult challenges to outright broken experiences, some games demand a level of dedication few players can truly muster. This list dives into titles that test the limits of player patience and perseverance.
en.body:
## 1. Bubsy 3D
Released in 1996, this platformer is a masterclass in how *not* to make a game, featuring famously awkward controls and a camera that actively works against you. Finishing Bubsy 3D feels less like a triumph and more like enduring a bizarre, frustrating punishment.

## 2. Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
FromSoftware games are known for their difficulty, but Sekiro's relentless boss encounters and demanding combat system pushed even seasoned players to their breaking point. While many *tried*, the sheer wall of challenge meant victory was a rare achievement earned through sheer grit.

## 3. Superman 64
Plagued by a perpetual fog that obscured vision and a control scheme that felt actively hostile, Superman 64 is infamous for its miserable gameplay. Most players likely rented it out of morbid curiosity and abandoned the quest to fly through rings long before the credits.

## 4. Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy
This physics-based indie darling is designed for maximum player frustration, where one wrong move can send you plummeting back down hours of painstaking progress. The game's appeal lies in its sheer, unadulterated rage-quitting potential, making full completion a badge of masochistic honor.

## 5. Dark Souls
The original Dark Souls set a new standard for punishing difficulty in 2011, a challenge that famously sent many players packing before they could truly experience its world. While fans revel in its demanding nature, the idea of anyone conquering its later bosses without significant mental fortitude remains a subject of debate.

## 6. Ride to Hell: Retribution
This 2013 action game is widely considered one of the worst of its generation, rife with bugs, nonsensical gameplay, and a story that fails to engage. Its sheer awfulness makes the prospect of playing through its entirety a Herculean task few would willingly undertake.

## 7. Superman 64 (N64)
Revisiting this 1999 title, its legacy as a broken experience is cemented by its infamous ring-collecting missions and a pervasive, game-breaking fog. It's a game that tested the patience of even the most dedicated Nintendo 64 owners, with many likely giving up before seeing the end.

## 8. Final Fantasy XIII
While a beloved franchise, Final Fantasy XIII's linear design and repetitive combat, released in 2009, proved divisive. Many players found the journey tedious, with the sheer length and lack of player freedom leading to significant drop-off rates before reaching Gran Pulse.

## 9. The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
Though a Nintendo staple, Skyward Sword's (2011) motion controls and repetitive item-finding quests frustrated many players. The reliance on precise, often finicky, waggle mechanics made progressing through its dungeons a chore for a significant portion of its audience.

## 10. Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
This 2001 sequel famously sidelined its beloved protagonist for a new character, Raiden, and threw players into a convoluted plot. The bait-and-switch, coupled with extended cutscenes and complex mechanics, led many to abandon the game before uncovering its full narrative.
Bottom Line: These games are less about finishing and more about surviving the experience.

tr.title: 10 Oyun Ki Tamamlayamadığınızdan Eminiz
tr.summary: Bu listede, bazı oyunlar var ki onları tamamlayabilmek için oyuncuların gerçekten çok fazla sabır ve azim göstermeleri gerekiyor. İşte, oyuncuların sabrını ve azmini test eden oyunlar.
tr.body:
## 1. Bubsy 3D
Bubsy 3D, 1996 yılında yayınlanan bir platform oyunu ve nasıl oyun yapılmaması gerektiğini gösteren bir örnek. Awkward kontrolleri ve size karşı çalışan kamera sistemiyle, Bubsy 3D'yi tamamlayabilmek bir zafer değil, daha çok bir ceza gibi geliyor.

## 2. Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
FromSoftware oyunları zaten zorluklarıyla tanınyor, ancak Sekiro'nun amansız boss karşılaşmaları ve zorlu savaş sistemi, deneyimli oyuncuları bile sınadı. Birçok oyuncu denedi, ancak zorluk duvarı öyle yüksek ki, zafer sadece azimle kazanılabiliyor.

## 3. Superman 64
Sürekli bir sis tarafından görüşünüzün engellenmesi ve düşmanca bir kontrol şemasıyla, Superman 64 kötü oyun deneyimiyle ünlü. Çoğu oyuncu muhtemelen meraktan oyunu kiraladı ve uzun süre önce kredileri görmeden oyunu bıraktı.

## 4. Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy
Bu fizik tabanlı indie oyun, maksimum oyuncu frustrasyonu için tasarlandı ve yanlış bir hareket, saatlerce emeğinizi boşa çıkarabilir. Oyunun çekiciliği, kızgınlıkla terk etme potansiyelinde yatıyor ve tamamlanması, bir tür mazohist onur madalyası gibi görünüyor.

## 5. Dark Souls
Orijinal Dark Souls, 2011 yılında zorluk standardını yükseltti ve birçok oyuncuyu,世界ını gerçekten deneyimlemeye başlamadan önce terk etmeye mecbur bıraktı. Hayranlar, zorlu doğasını seviyor, ancaklater boss'ları yenmek için gereken mental dayanıklılık, hala bir tartışma konusu.

## 6. Ride to Hell: Retribution
Bu 2013 aksiyon oyunu,广 olarak bu jenerasyonun en kötüsü olarak kabul ediliyor, hatalar, anlamsız oyun mekanikleri ve oyuncuyu bağlayamayan bir hikayesiyle. Kötülüğü, oyunu tamamlayabilmenin bir Herkül görevi gibi görünmesini sağlıyor.

## 7. Superman 64 (N64)
Bu 1999 oyununa döndüğümüzde, broken bir deneyim olarak ününü, ünlü yüzük toplama görevleriyle ve oyunu bozan bir sisle pekiştiriyor. Bu, Nintendo 64 sahiplerinin sabrını sınayan bir oyun ve birçok oyuncu muhtemelen bitmeden önce terk etti.

## 8. Final Fantasy XIII
Sevilen bir franchise olmasına rağmen, Final Fantasy XIII'ün lineer tasarımı ve tekrarlanan savaş mekanikleri, 2009 yılında yayınlandığında, bölücü oldu. Birçok oyuncu, yolculuğun sıkıcı buldu ve uzunluk ve oyuncu özgürlüğünün olmaması, birçok oyuncunun Gran Pulse'e ulaşmadan önce oyunu bırakmasına neden oldu.

## 9. The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
Nintendo'nun önemli bir parçası olmasına rağmen, Skyward Sword'un (2011) motion kontrolleri ve tekrarlanan item-bulma görevleri, birçok oyuncuyu frustrasyonla doldurdu. Precise ve often finicky waggle mekanikleri, dungeon'lardan ilerlemeyi bir görev haline getirdi.

## 10. Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
Bu 2001 devam oyunu, ünlü protagonistini bir kenara bırakarak yeni bir karakter, Raiden'i ortaya çıkardı ve oyuncuları karmaşık bir hikayeye attı. Bait-and-switch, uzun cutscene'lerle ve kompleks mekaniklerle birleşti ve birçok oyuncunun, hikayenin tamamını keşfetmeden önce oyunu terk etmesine neden oldu.

Sonuç: Bu oyunlar, tamamlayabilmek değil, deneyimi sağsalim atlatmak hakkında.

es.title: 10 Juegos que Es Probable que No Terminaras
es.summary: Desde desafíos notoriously difíciles hasta experiencias rotas, algunos juegos demandan una dedicación que pocos jugadores pueden realmente mantener. Esta lista explora títulos que ponen a prueba los límites de la paciencia y la perseverancia de los jugadores.
es.body:
## 1. Bubsy 3D

Lanzado en 1996, este plataformer es una clase maestra en cómo *no* hacer un juego, con controles famosamente torpes y una cámara que trabaja activamente en tu contra. Terminar Bubsy 3D siente menos como un triunfo y más como soportar una penalización extraña y frustrante.

## 2. Sekiro: Sombras que Muere Dos Veces

Los juegos de FromSoftware son conocidos por su dificultad, pero Sekiro's encuentros con jefes incesantes y su sistema de combate exigente empujaron incluso a los jugadores experimentados a su límite. Si bien muchos *trataron*, la pared de desafío significaba que la victoria era una logística rara ganada a través de la simpleza de la determinación.

## 3. Superman 64

Afectado por una niebla perpetua que obuscaba la visión y un esquema de control que sentía hostil, Superman 64 es infame por su juego miserable. La mayoría de los jugadores probablemente lo alquilaron por curiosidad morbosa y abandonaron la búsqueda de volar a través de anillos antes de las créditos.

## 4. Getting Over It con Bennett Foddy

Este indie físico encantador está diseñado para la frustración máxima del jugador, donde un movimiento incorrecto puede enviarlo volando hacia abajo horas de progreso laborioso. El atractivo de la partida radica en su potencial de quitar la ira pura, lo que hace la completa terminación una insignia de honor masoquista.

## 5. Dark Souls

El original Dark Souls estableció un nuevo estándar para la dificultad castigadora en 2011, un desafío que envió a muchos jugadores a su casa antes de que pudieran experimentar verdaderamente su mundo. Si bien los fans revuelven en su naturaleza exigente, la idea de que alguien conquistara a sus jefes posteriores sin un fortalecimiento mental significativo sigue siendo un tema de debate.

## 6. Ride to Hell: Retribución

Este juego de acción de 2013 es ampliamente considerado uno de los peores de su generación, lleno de bugs, juego incoherente y una historia que no engancha. Su mala calidad hace que la posibilidad de jugar a través de su totalidad sea una tarea hércules que pocos estarían dispuestos a emprender.

## 7. Superman 64 (N64)

Al revisitar este título de 1999, su legado como una experiencia rota está sellado por sus misiones de recolección de anillos infames y una niebla persistente, que rompe el juego. Es un juego que probó la paciencia incluso de los dueños más dedicados de Nintendo 64, con muchos probablemente abandonando antes de ver el final.

## 8. Final Fantasy XIII

Si bien una franquicia querida, Final Fantasy XIII's diseño lineal y combate repetitivo, lanzado en 2009, resultó divisivo. Muchos jugadores encontraron el viaje tedioso, con la longitud y falta de libertad del jugador conduciendo a tasas significativas de abandono antes de llegar a Gran Pulse.

## 9. The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword

Aunque un estandarte de Nintendo, Skyward Sword's (2011) controles de movimiento y misiones de búsqueda de objetos repetitivos frustraron a muchos jugadores. La dependencia de mecánicas de wobble precisas y a menudo finas hizo que avanzar a través de sus mazmorras fuera un trabajo para una parte significativa de su audiencia.

## 10. Metal Gear Solid 2: Hijos de la Libertad

Esta secuela de 2001 famosamente desplazó a su protagonista querido por un nuevo personaje, Raiden, y lanzó a los jugadores en una trama convulsa. La sorpresa y las escenas extendidas, junto con mecánicas complejas, llevaron a muchos a abandonar el juego antes de descubrir su narrativa completa.

En resumen: estos juegos son menos sobre terminar y más sobre sobrevivir la experiencia.

content_raw: Games are meant to be entertainment above all else, no matter what your idea of fun is. As such, there are certain video games that, for one reason or another, we don’t believe most people that say they played them, actually did. On the one hand, you have games known for being bad, broken, or oftentimes ‘unplayable,’ with only the most dedicated of gamers being able to push through them for one reason or another. On the other hand, you have games that are so hard, the level of dedication required to finish them often doesn’t align with having a job or career. These are the games we don’t believe most people finished. IMDb Bubsy 3D Often listed among the worst platformers ever made, Bubsy 3D became infamous for awkward controls, terrible camera angles, and bizarre voice lines. Finishing it feels less like beating a game and more like surviving a punishment challenge. IMDb Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice Yes, people absolutely finished Sekiro, but the game’s brutal bosses and precision-heavy combat convinced countless players they simply were not built for victory. Every win feels earned through equal parts skill, stubbornness, and emotional damage. IMDb Superman 64 Between endless fog, broken controls, and infamous ring-flying missions, Superman 64 gained a reputation as one of gaming’s most miserable experiences. Many players rented it out of curiosity and likely gave up before reaching the ending. YouTube/Bennett Foddy Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy Designed specifically to frustrate players, Getting Over It punishes mistakes by sending you crashing backward through hours of progress. The combination of brutal physics and sarcastic narration turned rage-quitting into the entire appeal. IMDb Dark Souls The original Dark Souls became legendary for difficulty so punishing that many players bounced off entirely. Fans love the challenge, but outsiders still look at late-game bosses and wonder whether anyone finished it without losing their sanity. IMDb Ride to Hell: Retribution This biker action game became notorious for broken combat, awkward dialogue, and bizarrely unfinished cutscenes. Critics destroyed it on release, and its reputation became so bad many people joke nobody ever willingly completed the entire thing. IMDb Battletoads The infamous Turbo Tunnel alone probably stopped generations of players from ever seeing the ending. Battletoads mixed fun co-op chaos with difficulty spikes so cruel that finishing it became a badge of honor. YouTube/NintendoComplete Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde This NES game confused players for decades thanks to strange mechanics, punishing enemy placement, and almost incomprehensible progression. Many likely spent more time wondering how it worked than actually making progress toward the ending.
